title: Heuristic v1
description: A domain-neutral behavioral rule with evidence support, scope, and a rollback path (ADR-0007 decision 7). Lifecycle transitions are append-only: each transition is a new record version with a new heuristic_id, an ID-only supersedes pointer, a status snapshot, and a mandatory transition rationale. The Phase 4 ceiling is shadow: validated, promoted, deprecated, and retired exist in the vocabulary so later phases need no schema change, but are unreachable in this phase; shadow heuristics only record hypothetical decisions and never change production behavior.

statement.description: The rule itself, stated as a falsifiable behavioral statement.

mode.description: advisory rules only annotate; blocking rules halt the guarded action. A blocking rule whose rollback is vacuous is rejected by the registry linter (acceptance gate 8); rollback is nevertheless a required field for every mode so the rejection surface stays explicit.

evidence.description: Evidence summaries supporting this heuristic; at least one. The underlying evidence records stay reachable through regression_cases and their case packages.

exception.description: Known exceptions where the rule does not apply. May be an explicit empty array.

risk.description: What goes wrong if this rule misfires.

rollback.description: How to undo the effect of applying this rule. Mandatory for every mode (plan Phase 4 task 12).

status.description: Snapshot of this version's lifecycle state (plan Phase 4 task 13, underscore style). The Phase 4 ceiling is shadow (plan section 3.2); later states are vocabulary only in this phase.

transition_rationale.description: Why this version exists. Mandatory for every version, including the initial one.

regression_cases.description: Regression cases demonstrating the lesson, each hash-pinned to research-case-package/v2 records; at least one (plan Phase 4 task 15). The mandatory association fails closed at the schema layer.

supersedes.description: Optional heuristic_id of the prior version this one supersedes. ID-only lineage reference within the heuristic family; earlier versions are never edited in place.
